earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct unclassified Brazilian language known only from a short wordlist; no phonological description exists.

sources.note: No descriptive references at all (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); only Wikipedia/Wikidata links.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Baenã language' (accessed 2026-09-17); cites Loukotka 1963, Meader 1978, Nelson 2018.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; reproduces the 9-word list (secondary) and reports that by 1961 the last Baenã person, Rosalinda, could not provide any words of the language (citing Meader 1978).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. p. 74, entry '21. Baenan, isolated language'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the entry gives only location ('originally spoken between the Cachoeira and Pardo Rivers, state of Bahia, now only by a few individuals on the Posto Paraguaçú') and cites Loukotka 1963 p. 54 and 'Nimuendajú ms.n.'; no words, no phonology.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1963. Documents et vocabulaires inédits de langues et de dialectes sud-américains. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 52: 7-60. §62 'Langue dont le nom indigène est inconnu', p. 54.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Prints the 9 words Nimuendajú recorded in 1938 (from his notebook 'Kamakan-Material II', SPI archive, Rio), which R. D. Carneiro attributed to the Baenan tribe: eželẽ 'cerf', bakurí 'chevreuil', kelemés 'feu', patarak 'jaguar', kadašužé 'nègre', bonikro 'porc', pititiŋga 'rat', pitirát 'singe', šẽšẽ 'taureau'. Four words carry an acute accent on the final syllable, five carry no mark; no note on what the accents mean and no remark on stress anywhere in the article (pp. 7-8 introduction checked). sources.citation: Nelson, Jessica Fae. 2018. Pataxó Hãhãhãe: Race, Indigeneity and Language Revitalization in the Brazilian Northeast. PhD dissertation, University of Arizona.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern ethnographic/sociolinguistic account of the Pataxó Hãhãhãe, of whom the Baenã are now a subgroup; may summarize the historical record of Baenã but cannot contain new phonological data.

sources.citation: Meader, Robert E. 1978. Indios do Nordeste: levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro. (Série Lingüística 8.) Brasília: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL survey of remnant groups of the Northeast; per Wikipedia it records that the last Baenã person (Rosalinda, 1961) could give no words, so it likely contains no Baenã data, but it should be checked for any residual forms or remarks.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1938. 'Kamakan-Material II', manuscript notebook, formerly SPI central archive, Rio de Janeiro (now presumably Museu do Índio / Nimuendajú papers).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The sole primary record of the 9 words; the original could show whether the acute accents are Nimuendajú's stress marks and whether any note on accent accompanies them. Would not yield a general stress rule.
